## Milestone 1 - Task 3.3: Response Normalizer

Consumes whatever `03-http-executor` produced - a successful HTTP Response Contract (docs/contracts/http-response-contract.md) or an ERROR payload for a transport failure (timeout, connection refused, DNS failure, pre-flight validation) - and normalizes both into one stable Normalized Response Contract (docs/contracts/normalized-response-contract.md).

The Decision Agent (Task 4, not yet built) never sees a raw HTTP response and never knows which HTTP client executed the request - this workflow is that boundary. It never compares against `expected`, never decides PASS/FAIL, and never calls an AI model - those stay the Decision Agent's job.

A transport failure is not a failure of THIS workflow - it is normalized into `transport.status: "TIMEOUT"` / `"NETWORK_ERROR"` / etc., same as any other result. Only a genuinely malformed or unrecognizable input produces this workflow's own shared ERROR payload.

## Task 3.3 design notes

- `__kind` (`'error'` or `'response'`) is set once, by `Validate Contract`, and is the only thing every later node checks to decide whether it's still looking at an in-progress item or has already produced this workflow's own ERROR payload (`!item.__kind` = short-circuit, pass through unchanged). This mirrors the `status === 'ERROR'` early-return convention in 01/02/03, but can't reuse that exact check here - a transport failure from 03 already has `status: 'ERROR'` and is exactly the input this workflow is supposed to normalize, not pass through.
- `TRANSPORT_CODE_MAP` in `Normalize Transport` is a hand-kept allow-list mapping every `03-http-executor` error `code` to a transport category, same pattern as `SUPPORTED_VERIFICATION_TYPES`/`AGENT_ROUTES` in `01-ingestion.json` (docs/workflow-standards.md). A `03-http-executor` code with no entry here produces `UNKNOWN_TRANSPORT_ERROR` rather than a silent guess.
- `request_id`/`test_case`/`expected` are read from `item.details` on the transport-failure path (03 v1.1 carries them there) and from the top level on the successful-response path - see docs/contracts/http-response-contract.md's versioning notes.

nodes.notes: Hand-off boundary to the Decision Agent workflow (Task 4, not yet built). Receives either a Normalized Response Contract (docs/contracts/normalized-response-contract.md) or an ERROR payload (docs/contracts/error-payload.md) for input this workflow itself could not normalize. No PASS/FAIL judgment or AI reasoning happens in this workflow.
